newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Hospital catches fire in Philippine earthquake.
newsitem.headline: Hospital catches fire in Philippine earthquake.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale hit the southern Philippine island of Mindanao on Wednesday, triggering a fire that damaged a hospital building but there were no reports of casualties, officials said.

The third floor of the Capital College General Hospital in Cagayan de Oro City, about 750 km (465 miles) south of Manila, was destroyed in the fire caused by an electrical short-circuit during the earthquake, fire investigator Maximo Carreon said by telephone.
Rescue workers evacuated 29 patients from the floor but there were no casualties, he said.

Cagayan de Oro is about 200 km (125 miles) east of the coastal town of Lingig, believed to be closest to the epicentre of the earthquake. There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage in Lingig.
Chief government seismologist Delfin Garcia said the tremor measured 7.0 on the Richter scale and was centered in the sea.
"It came from a depth of about 100 km (60 miles) and we don't expect any major damage or calamity because it was so deep," he said.
The earthquake occurred at 3:21 a.m. (1921 GMT Tuesday) and was felt in several cities and towns on Mindanao, 800 km (500 miles) south of Manila, Garcia said.
Officials in Cagayan de Oro said the hospital fire was put out within an hour. A building adjoining the hospital had developed some cracks, they added.
Officials in nearby Butuan town said there were no reports of damage.
"It wasn't strong. We always have these frequent quakes but they are not that strong," senior superintendent of police Alberto Olario told Reuters by telephone.

"Aftershocks and damage are expected to be minimal due to the tremor's depth from the surface and distance from densely populated areas," said a bulletin from the Philippine Institute of Vulcanology and Seismology.
About 1,600 people died in July 1990 when an earthquake measuring 7.7 struck the main Philippine island of Luzon.
